decisions.descriptionMarkdown: `src/release.rs` (public module `release`): `Release` (parsed `semver::Version` without prerelease or build part, `Display` as `X.Y.Z`), `parse(&str) -> Result<Release, ReleaseError>`, `Release::direction(from, to) -> Direction::{Upgrade, Same, Downgrade}`, `installer_url(&Release) -> String`, `MIN_REFRESH_RELEASE`, and `exists(&mut Runner, &Release) -> Existence::{Exists, Missing, Unknown(String)}` over `curl --proto =https --tlsv1.2 -sfIL <url>` (curl exit 22 is a 404). `setup::guest` takes its release base URL and installer URL from here (the `RELEASES` constant moves; `tests/release_automation.rs` keeps checking the `{RELEASES}/v{version}/` form in the file that now owns it). `semver` is already a dependency.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - One definition of the installer URL and of what a release name is.\n- `exists` only reads (headers), through `Runner::query`.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: `self update`, the guest install and the refresh all need to parse, order and check releases; without one owner each would grow its own rules. A HEAD request avoids downloading the installer to learn that a tag exists, and curl is already what the guest install uses.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: `SelfCommand::Update` gains `--release <X.Y.Z>` (not `--version`: `propagate_version` reserves it on every subcommand). `update::Backend` gains `install_release(&Release) -> Result<Version, String>` next to `install()`; the real backend sets `UpdateRequest::SpecificVersion` and `always_update(true)` (axoupdater otherwise refuses a downgrade) before `run_sync`. `run_with_refresh` takes the requested release: it compares with the installed version (`Direction`), asks the downgrade question through the existing `Refresher::confirm`, applies the receipt rule, and offers the refresh only when the new version is at least `MIN_REFRESH_RELEASE`. The plain path (no `--release`) keeps its code and tests. Nothing is persisted.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - A `rayx` without an install receipt is never replaced.\n- `--check` never installs; a refused downgrade changes nothing.\n- The refresh runs the executable captured before the install.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: axoupdater already supports a specific version and downgrades, so no download or archive code is added; the receipt keeps `self update` safe for development builds.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: `--release <X.Y.Z>` on `SetupArgs` (requires `lima`, `wsl` or `update`, conflicts with the sets that make no sense). `LinuxBinary.version` is the chosen release instead of the running version; `guest::ensure_linux_binary` already compares `rayx --version` with it and installs the tag's installer, so a different release (older or newer) is replaced. A `ReleasePlan { release, existence }` is computed once at the start of `setup::lima::run_with`, `setup::wsl::run_with` and `setup::refresh::refresh_guests` by `release::exists`, before any change. The guest downgrade question reuses `Prompter`. In the refresh, the inner `setup --update` is skipped when the release is below `MIN_REFRESH_RELEASE`. The chosen release is not stored in `guests.json` or `setup.json`.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - Existence is checked before any VM, distribution, record or install change.\n- A release override and a binary override (`RAYX_*_BINARY`) never combine.\n- Nothing about the chosen release is recorded.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The guest layer already installs by version through the release installer, so the choice is one parameter; skipping the inner update for releases that lack the flag is what the Windows proof of the guest epic showed is needed (`unexpected argument '--update'`).

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: The Lima instance name becomes a value (`VmName`: validated, default `rayx`, `Display`, derived names `<name>-<version>`) threaded through `setup::lima::{run_with, ensure_lima, apply_edit, record_failed_first_run}`, `setup::migrate::{LimaMigration, LimaOld, pending_lima, migrate_lima}`, `setup::refresh`, `setup::remove`, `doctor::guests` and `guest::Guest::lima(name)`; the `INSTANCE` constant remains only as the default. Before any change `run_with` lists instances strictly and refuses a name that exists in Lima but is not a recorded Lima guest (`never adopt`). `pending_lima` matches retired `migrating` entries named `<name>-<version>` for the given name only. `--vm` is `Vec<String>` on `SetupArgs` (`requires` `lima` or `update`, conflicts with `wsl`); with `setup --lima` more than one value is refused.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - Only recorded guests, and the VM being created under the requested name, are touched.\n- A name never matches another name's retired or migrating entries.\n- The default name keeps every earlier behaviour (arguments, messages, records).
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The single-VM epic fixed the name `rayx` in many places; the owner wants one VM per project repository. Refusing to adopt unrecorded VMs is the safe generalisation (`gpux`-shaped VMs must be unreachable by a typo), and it supersedes the promoted decision's phrase that only the instance named `rayx` is created and changed.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: `setup::update::run` and `refresh_guests` take a target filter (`Option<Vec<VmName>>`): with a filter only the named recorded current guests are refreshed (Lima and WSL alike, matching by recorded name) and `update_host` is skipped; an unknown name is an error listing the recorded current guests, raised before any command. With `--release`, the target guests get that release (d-guest-release). `self update`'s refresh offer keeps refreshing everything.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - An explicit target never touches other guests or the host.\n- Validation of names happens before the first command.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: With one VM per project, refreshing the whole fleet to test one project's release is the wrong default for an explicit request.
